findings.title: All success criteria map to tasks; no gaps
findings.description: Functional Requirements 1–11 are covered: empty/scaffold-only (Task 12 fixtures 1–2), brownfield detection + state write (fixture 3, Task 9T), shallow clone (fixture 4, Task 5T), concept-only + code (fixture 6), planned (fixture 7, Task 9T walk-never-runs), monorepo scoping (fixture 5), `in_progress` resume (fixture 8), override transitions (fixture 9, Task 1T for enum rejection), `--phase 2` and explicit `--it brownfield-adoption` (fixtures 10–11), `template_preview` non-write (fixture 13), guide-missing profile/prompt (fixture 12, Task 9T). Technical Requirements are covered by T-tasks (3T, 4T, 5T, 6T, 7T, 8T, 9T), Task 12, Task 13, Task 15. Integration Requirements are satisfied architecturally (Task 8's exported `renderSquadronFact` for 262; Task 2's `readAdoptionState`/`writeAdoptionState` for 263/264; Task 15 step 1 for the byte-identical planned-project assertion).

findings.title: Sequencing and test-with-implement pattern respected
findings.description: Each implementation task is immediately followed by its test task (3→3T, 4→4T, 5→5T, 6→6T, 7→7T, 8→8T, 9→9T, 10→10T). The dependency chain runs cleanly: contracts/state (Tasks 1–2) before detection facts (Tasks 3–6) before outcome/facts (Tasks 7–8) before resolver/integration (Tasks 9–11) before integration tests and walkthrough (Tasks 12–15). No circular dependencies.

findings.title: Commit markers at working, tested points
findings.description: The `**Commit**:` lines (2C, 3C, 5C, 6C, 8C, 9C, 11C, 13C, 14C, 15C) are plain text (no checkboxes), placed after the corresponding implementation + tests. They group cohesive work (e.g. 5C bundles Tasks 4–5 as "present-path and history detection facts"; 8C bundles Tasks 7–8 as "outcome decision and facts renderer"; 11C bundles Tasks 10–11 as the `cf build` and `context_build` wiring).

findings.title: Sub-second NFR verified by cap tests, not a load test
findings.description: The slice design restates a sub-second detection NFR (D2: "detection adds under one second to a Phase 0 build on a local disk") and explicitly resolves it with cap tests rather than timings: "Tests assert the caps, not timings." The task breakdown honors that decision via Task 3T's early-exit and `MAX_WALK_ENTRIES` cases, and the task file's Context Summary documents the rationale (the `tests/load/` tier is `rules/python.md`-only). No load test task is required by the slice design's own decision; flagging this only so reviewers see the linkage between the NFR and the cap-based verification.

findings.title: Resolver import direction enforced
findings.description: Task 10 explicitly states `ContextIntegrator.ts` imports `AdoptionResolver` and `AdoptionError` from `../adoption/contracts.js` only (never from `adoption/index.ts`), and the Context Summary pre-records the F005 import-cycle review (`contracts.ts` imports nothing; `createAdoptionResolver` is wired in `CoreServiceFactory.ts`). The ConfigManager↔adoptionState cycle is resolved by defining `ADOPTION_STATES`/`AdoptionState` in `config/ConfigKeys.ts` and re-exporting from `adoption/adoptionState.ts`.
